questions.question: Returning patient with an Acinetobacter resistant to everything in a post fracture wound.

parts.text: Indicate two mechanisms of resistance to carbapenems
Give two alternatives for antibiotic treatment

cohort_answer.text:
Two mechanisms of resistance: Carbapenemase production; Efflux pump; Change in PBPs
Two alternatives: Colistin; Tigecycline

parts.text: a) What is the mechanism of carbapenem resistance?
b) What is the preferred treatment if carbapenems cannot be used?

cohort_answer.text:
OXA-51 Carbapenemase – intrinsic/chromosomal, often expressed poorly. Efflux pump also common (resistance to B-lactam, chloramphenicol, macrolides, tetracycline, aminoglycosides). Acquired carbapenemases: Ambler Class B MBL (emerging): IMP (plasmids), VIM (more common), NDM; OXA-48 (Class D)
Rate of MDR <10-15% and not critical illness: cefepime 2g IV q8h or meropenem 2g IV q8h infused over 3 hrs. Rate of MDR >10-15% and/or critical illness: consider combo of amp-sulbactam + mero + polymyxin B (can also use colistin and tige)

questions.question: A multi-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumanii resistant to all beta-lactams, septra, FQ

parts.text: What are two mechanisms that lead to carbapenem resistance?
What 2 treatment options can be used?

questions.model_answer:
a) 2 mechanisms of carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii: (1) production of carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D beta-lactamases (OXA-type carbapenemases, e.g., OXA-23, OXA-24/40, OXA-58); (2) decreased outer membrane permeability (porin loss) combined with upregulated efflux pump activity (e.g., AdeABC efflux system) - metallo-beta-lactamase production (e.g., NDM, VIM) is an additional accepted mechanism.
b) 2 treatment options: (1) polymyxins (colistin or polymyxin B); (2) high-dose ampicillin-sulbactam (sulbactam has intrinsic antibacterial activity against Acinetobacter) - cefiderocol is another accepted modern option.

questions.question: Q36 (2015). Antibacterial Mechanism of Resistance. A multi-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii is resistant to all beta-lactams, septra, FQ

parts.text: a) What are 2 mechanisms that lead to carbapenem resistance?
b) What 2 tx options can be used?

cohort_answer.text: a) Beta-lactamases hydrolyzing carbapenems: Ambler class D oxacillinases (OXAs) group 2d (OXA-51-like intrinsic/chromosomal; acquired OXA subclasses on chromosomes/plasmids, zinc-dependent metalloenzymes); intrinsic class B beta-lactamases (Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, Elizabethkingia meningoseptica); acquired class B beta-lactamases (VIM, NDM); Ambler Class A beta-lactamases (KPCs). Also porins (diminished permeability from impaired OMP expression) and efflux of drugs across outer membrane. b) Tigecycline or Minocycline; Colistin or polymyxin B; continuous/extended intermittent beta-lactam infusion; local instillation of colistin (intrathecal for CNS); combination therapy (colistin + minocycline/tigecycline/carbapenem/rifampin); newer agents (ceftazidime-avibactam, ceftolozane-tazobactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam, plazomicin, eravacycline, cefiderocol, IV fosfomycin).

questions.question: Q51 (2008). Antibacterial Mechanism of Resistance. Canadian soldier returning from Afghanistan with wound infection/cellulitis. Grows Acinetobacter - resistant to Mero/Imi, SXT, Chloramphenicol, Doxy

parts.text: a) What are two mechanisms of resistance to carbapenems?
b) What are two treatment options?

cohort_answer.text: a) Enzyme inhibition (metallo-beta-lactamases, OXA-type serine carbapenemases); reduced outer membrane permeability (efflux pumps). b) Tigecycline; Colistin; Fluoroquinolones.

Q58 (2011 PM)
Soldier from abroad (Afghanistan) with non-healing wounds on PipTazo and Vanco. Traumatic ulcers to legs with surrounding cellulitis worsening on PipTazo/Vanco. Swab grows GNB resistant to all carbapenems, cephalosporins, AG and FQ

Soldier from abroad (Afghanistan) with non-healing wounds on PipTazo and Vanco. Traumatic ulcers to legs with surrounding cellulitis worsening on piptazo/vanco. Swab grows GNB with resistance to all carbapenems, cephalosporins, aminoglycosides, and quinolones.

parts.text: What drugs can you use to treat?

cohort_answer.text: Acinetobacter baumannii. Treatment: High dose amp-sulbactam, Tigecycline/minocycline, Colistin/polymyxin B; rifamycins not recommended (insufficient evidence); extended infusion meropenem (combined with other agents), local instillation, phage therapy

questions.question: Tigecycline, Septra, imipenem vs Acinetobacter, Pseudomonas, Stenotrophomonas.  Which bugs are intrinsically resistant to which agents?

parts.text: Which bugs are intrinsically resistant to which agents? (Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Stenotrophomonas)

cohort_answer.text:
Pseudo: R- Tigecycline, R- Septra, S-Imipenem
Acinetobacter: S- Septra, S- tige, S- Imi
Steno: R- Imipenem, S- tigecycline, S- Septra

questions.question: Q45 (2012 AM). Antibacterial Mechanism of Resistance. Chart to fill in (R or S): | Tigecycline | Ertapenem | Colistin for Acinetobacter, Stenotrophomonas, Pseudomonas, Proteus, ESBL

cohort_answer.text: Acinetobacter | S | R | S. Stenotrophomonas | S | R | S. Pseudomonas | R | R | S. Proteus | R | S | R. ESBL | S | S | S.
